mainTopic: Defects in an אתרוג: holes, internal rot, color, and unripeness
overview: This amud opens by settling a contradiction about a peeled אתרוג: the משנה means a fully peeled one, and רבא means a partly peeled one. עולא בר חנינא then teaches that a hole going all the way through disqualifies at any size, but a shallow hole only at the size of an איסר. רבא asks what happens if 'signs of a טרפה' appear in an אתרוג. The גמרא explains that he means an אתרוג that liquefied inside, like a liquefied lung, which רבי יוחנן rules כשר as long as its bronchia are intact. The question is whether the lung heals only because it is sealed from air, while an exposed אתרוג would rot. A ברייתא listing disqualified kinds of אתרוג is brought as a proof, but the proof is rejected, because תפוח and סרוח can both describe outside problems. The גמרא then reconciles two ברייתות about a כושי אתרוג. אביי and רבא each give their own answer. Finally, רבה links רבי עקיבא's ruling on an unripe אתרוג to רבי שמעון's exemption of small אתרוגים from מעשרות, and אביי shows that each ruling may rest on its own separate reason.

steps.title: Fully peeled versus partly peeled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the conflict between the משנה (peeled is פסול) and רבא (peeled is כשר). One case is fully peeled, the other only partly peeled.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (the משנה) is when all of it is peeled. That one (רבא) is when only part of it is peeled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes resolving a contradiction raised on the previous amud. It explains that the two rulings about a peeled אתרוג are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a peeled אתרוג is פסול, but רבא said a peeled אתרוג is כשר. The answer is that they are not arguing. A fully peeled אתרוג is פסול, while one peeled only in part stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This one… that one': a formula for splitting two sources into two different cases
all of it, the whole thing

steps.whatToRemember: Peeling disqualifies an אתרוג only when the whole אתרוג is peeled. Partial peeling leaves it כשר.

phrases.english: This one is where all of it was peeled,
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה, which rules a peeled אתרוג פסול.

phrases.english: that one is where only part of it was peeled.
phrases.notes: Refers to רבא's statement that a peeled אתרוג is כשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised at the end of the previous amud (35b) between the משנה, which rules a peeled אתרוג פסול, and רבא, who rules it כשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): the two sources are about different amounts of peeling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבא seemed to give opposite rulings on the same case of a peeled אתרוג.
steps.terutzMaskana: Full peeling makes it פסול. Partial peeling leaves it כשר.

steps.title: How big a hole disqualifies an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next cases (split, pierced). Then עולא בר חנינא teaches that a hole going all the way through disqualifies at any size, but a hole that does not go through disqualifies only at the size of an איסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'split, pierced.' עולא בר חנינא taught: if it was pierced with a hole that goes all the way through, any size makes it פסול. If the hole does not go all the way through, it is פסול only when the hole is the size of an איסר coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next words of the משנה, 'split' and 'pierced.' It brings a ברייתא that explains how big a hole must be to make an אתרוג פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just says 'pierced' without giving a size. עולא בר חנינא adds the detail. A hole all the way through is serious enough that even a tiny one disqualifies. A shallow hole needs to be as big as an איסר.

keyTerms.meaning: a small coin, used as a size measure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the through-hole needs to be bigger because it is deeper. It is the opposite: a hole that goes all the way through disqualifies at ANY size, and only the shallow hole needs to reach the size of an איסר.

phrases.english: The משנה says: 'split, pierced.'
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of the משנה being discussed.

phrases.english: Ulla bar Chanina taught:
If it was pierced with a hole that goes all the way through, it is unfit with any size hole,
and if the hole does not go through, it is unfit only at the size of an issar.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִסְדַּק, נִיקַּב. תָּנֵי עוּלָּא בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A through-hole disqualifies at any size. A non-through hole disqualifies only at the size of an איסר.

steps.title: רבא asks about signs of a טרפה in an אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the law is if signs of a טרפה develop in an אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if the signs of a טרפה developed in an אתרוג, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question. He asks whether the defects that make an animal a טרפה would also make an אתרוג פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of the אתרוג's defects (holes, missing parts) look like the defects that make an animal a טרפה. רבא wants to know whether we can borrow the טרפה rules for the אתרוג. The question itself is still vague, so the גמרא will need to clarify it next.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Rava raised a dilemma:
If signs of a tereifa developed in the etrog, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: נוֹלְדוּ בָּאֶתְרוֹג סִימָנֵי טְרֵפָה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, related to the defects just discussed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the טרפה defects of an animal also make an אתרוג פסול?

steps.title: Those cases are already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's question. Peeling, splitting, and piercing are all already taught in the משנה, so what new case is he asking about?
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is he asking? If it is a peeled אתרוג, we already learned that! If it is a split one, we already learned that! If it is a pierced one, we already learned that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's question. The obvious טרפה-like defects are already covered by the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Peeled skin, a crack, and a hole all resemble טרפה defects, and the משנה already rules on each. So רבא's question would be pointless unless he means some other case. This challenge forces the גמרא to define his question more precisely.

keyTerms.meaning: we already learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.english: What is he asking about?
If it was peeled, we learned that!
If it was split, we learned that!
If it was pierced, we learned that!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ? אִי נִקְלַף — תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's question has any new content.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about טרפה signs in an אתרוג
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every obvious case is already answered in the משנה, so the question seems to have no case left to ask about.

steps.title: He means a lung that liquefied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא is asking about a case like רבי יוחנן's ruling that a lung which liquefied 'like a pitcher' is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is asking about a case like what עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a lung that can be poured out like a pitcher is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the case רבא really means. It is not a hole or crack, but an inside that has turned to liquid, like a melted lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן rules that an animal whose lung tissue has dissolved into liquid is still כשר. The parallel in an אתרוג would be one that has gone liquid inside while its outside stays whole. The משנה never addresses that case, so this is a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: when he asks, it is about…

steps.confusionAlert: Surprisingly, רבי יוחנן says this liquefied lung is כשר, not a טרפה. That surprising leniency is exactly why the question about the אתרוג comes up.

phrases.english: When he raises the dilemma, it is
like what Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A lung that can be poured out like a pitcher is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ כִּדְעוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by naming a case not covered by the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the question: רבא means internal liquefaction, which parallels the lung case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that all טרפה-type defects of an אתרוג were already covered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about an אתרוג that liquefied inside, like the lung of רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבא's condition: the bronchia must be intact
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רבי יוחנן's leniency. The liquefied lung is כשר only if its bronchial tubes are still intact. Otherwise it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: this is only when the bronchial tubes are intact. But if the bronchial tubes are not intact, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבא's qualification to the lung ruling. This finishes setting up the background before the actual question about the אתרוג is asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's leniency has a limit. As long as the lung's 'skeleton,' the bronchial tubes, survives, the animal is כשר. If those are gone too, it is a טרפה. This fills in the full lung rule that the אתרוג question will be compared to.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
And that is only where its bronchia are intact.
But if its bronchia are not intact, it is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבי יוחנן's ruling, completing the background for the question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A liquefied lung is כשר only if the bronchial tubes are intact. Otherwise it is a טרפה.

steps.title: Does exposure to air make the אתרוג different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the precise question. A lung may be able to heal because it is sealed inside the body, but an אתרוג is exposed to air and will rot. Or perhaps there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law here, with the אתרוג? Maybe there, with the lung, the air does not reach it, so it can heal. But here, where the air reaches it, it will surely rot. Or maybe there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out both sides of רבא's question in its final, precise form. It compares a liquefied lung to an אתרוג that liquefied inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung is כשר because, sealed off from air, it can recover. If that is the reason, an אתרוג exposed to air would rot, and so it should be פסול. The other side says the cases are the same, so an אתרוג with its inner structure intact stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: the air has control over it, affects it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's question about טרפה signs in an אתרוג is really about internal liquefaction. The key issue is whether the lung's leniency depends on being sealed from air, which an אתרוג is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא compares cases by finding the reason behind a ruling (here, the ability to heal), not just the outward similarity between them.

phrases.english: Here, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא הָתָם הוּא דְּלָא שָׁלֵיט בַּהּ אַוֵּירָא,
phrases.english: Perhaps it is there, where the air does not affect it,
that it recovers,
but here, where the air affects it,
it will surely decay,
or perhaps it is no different?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מַאי? דִּלְמָא הָתָם הוּא דְּלָא שָׁלֵיט בַּהּ אַוֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the lung background to the אתרוג and spells out the two sides of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the liquefied-lung leniency based on being sealed from air (so an exposed אתרוג is different), or does it apply to an אתרוג as well?

steps.title: A ברייתא listing the disqualified kinds of אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists many kinds of פסול אתרוג. The goal is to use it to answer רבא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: An אתרוג that is swollen, rotted, pickled, boiled, black, white, or spotted is פסול. An אתרוג round like a ball is פסול, and some say a twin (two grown together) is also פסול. About an unripe אתרוג, רבי עקיבא says it is פסול and the חכמים say it is כשר. If someone grew it in a mold and made it look like a different kind of fruit, it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a possible source to answer רבא's question. This step only quotes the source. The actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is a list of things that make an אתרוג פסול. Two words in it, תפוח and סרוח, will be the key to the attempted proof. The other items, כושי and בוסר, will be discussed later in the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This phrase introduces a source brought as a proof.
A twin: two אתרוגים grown stuck together

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An etrog that is swollen, rotted,
pickled, boiled,
black, white, or spotted is unfit.
phrases.notes: Each of these makes the אתרוג not look like a normal, beautiful אתרוג.

phrases.english: An etrog round like a ball is unfit,
and some say: even a twin (is unfit).
An unripe etrog:
Rabbi Akiva rules it unfit, and the Sages rule it fit.
If he grew it in a mold
and made it look like a different kind of creation, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question stated in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Whether an אתרוג that rotted on the inside, like a liquefied lung, is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא listing disqualified kinds of אתרוג, especially the words תפוח and סרוח

steps.title: Reading swollen as outside and rotted as inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that תפוח means rot on the outside and סרוח means rot on the inside. If so, inner rot makes an אתרוג פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches 'swollen, rotted.' Doesn't this mean swollen on the outside and rotted on the inside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the actual proof from the ברייתא. It argues that the two words describe two different places: outside and inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two words that sound alike. The גמרא assumes each must teach something new, so one must be about the outside and one about the inside. That would mean inside rot makes the אתרוג פסול, which answers רבא's question: an אתרוג does not get the leniency of the lung.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This points to the specific words that matter for the proof.
Isn't it that...? This introduces a suggested reading that would prove the point.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches 'swollen, rotted.'
Is it not that 'swollen' means on the outside,
and 'rotted' means on the inside!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת תָּפוּחַ סָרוּחַ, מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: An אתרוג that rotted on the inside is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two separate words תפוח and סרוח in the ברייתא

steps.title: Both words describe the outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Both words are about the outside: one is swelling without rot, the other is rot without swelling.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both are about the outside. And it is not a problem that there are two words: one is where it swelled even though it did not rot, and the other is where it rotted even though it did not swell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. It shows another way to read the two words so that neither one is about the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that the two words must refer to two places. The גמרא shows they can be two different outside problems: swelling alone, or rot alone. So the ברייתא says nothing about inside rot, and רבא's question stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both cases
And it is not a difficulty

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean inner rot is כשר. It only means this ברייתא does not prove the answer either way. רבא's question is still open.

phrases.english: No, both this and that are on the outside,
and it is not a difficulty:

phrases.aramaic: הָא דִּתְפַח אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא סְרַח,
phrases.english: this is where it swelled, even though it did not rot,

phrases.aramaic: הָא דִּסְרַח אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא תְּפַח.
phrases.english: that is where it rotted, even though it did not swell.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. It does not decide the law of an אתרוג rotted inside.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the two words must mean outside and inside. They can instead be two different outside problems.
steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to answer רבא from the ברייתא fails. Both תפוח and סרוח are outside problems, so the question about inside rot is not resolved here.

steps.title: Contradiction about a black אתרוג
steps.stepSummary: Our ברייתא says a כושי אתרוג is פסול. Another ברייתא says a כושי is כשר and only one that looks like a כושי is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: a black אתרוג is פסול. But another ברייתא teaches: a black one is כשר, and one that only looks like a black one is פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to another line in the same ברייתא. It points out that a different ברייתא seems to say the opposite about a black אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא we quoted says כושי is פסול. The other ברייתא says a real כושי is כשר, and only an אתרוג that looks like a כושי is פסול. These two sources clash.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said. This quotes a line from the source just mentioned, in order to discuss it.
But was it not taught in a ברייתא? This introduces a contradicting source.
Looks like a black one, but is not truly that kind

phrases.english: The Master said: a black etrog is unfit.
But was it not taught: a black one is fit,
and one that looks like a black one is unfit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אֶתְרוֹג כּוּשִׁי — פָּסוּל. וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבא's question and examines another detail of the ברייתא from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in our ברייתא that a כושי אתרוג is פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says a real כושי is כשר and only one that looks like a כושי is פסול.

steps.title: אביי: our source also means one that looks like a כושי
steps.stepSummary: אביי says our source also really means 'looks like a כושי.' So both sources agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: When we learned it in our source too, we learned 'looks like a black one.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction. He reads our source as speaking about an אתרוג that only looks black, not a real כושי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי there is no real argument. A true כושי, a dark kind of אתרוג, is כשר. An ordinary אתרוג that turned black-looking is פסול, and that is what our source meant.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
When we learned our teaching too,
we learned 'looks like a black one.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our source said a real כושי is פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our source means one that looks like a כושי, so both sources agree that a real כושי is כשר.

steps.title: רבא: the ruling depends on the place
steps.stepSummary: רבא says each source is right for a different place. In בבל a כושי is פסול; in ארץ ישראל it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not a difficulty. This ruling (פסול) is for us, and that ruling (כשר) is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He keeps the plain meaning of both sources and says they apply in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל most אתרוגים are light, so a dark one looks strange and is פסול. In ארץ ישראל dark אתרוגים are common, so a כושי looks normal and is כשר. The ruling depends on what a normal אתרוג looks like in that place.

keyTerms.meaning: This is for us, meaning in בבל
And that is for them, meaning in ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's answer shows that 'what looks normal' can depend on the local fruit. The same color can be fine in one place and strange in another.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not a difficulty.
This is for us, and that is for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא לַן, וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than אביי to the contradiction in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources argue about a real כושי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are right. A כושי is פסול in בבל, where it looks unusual, and כשר in ארץ ישראל, where it is common.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says a real כושי is always כשר and only one that 'looks like' a כושי is פסול. רבא says a real כושי is פסול in בבל and כשר in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבה links רבי עקיבא to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line about an unripe אתרוג. רבה says רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון hold the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unripe אתרוג: רבי עקיבא says פסול, and the חכמים say כשר. רבה said: רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון said the same thing. רבי עקיבא's view is the one we just mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא, about an unripe אתרוג. רבה makes a claim that sets up the next step, where רבי שמעון's source is shown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says an unripe אתרוג is פסול for the מצוה. רבה says this comes from the same idea as a ruling by רבי שמעון. The idea is that an unripe אתרוג is not yet considered a real fruit.

phrases.english: An unripe etrog:
Rabbi Akiva rules it unfit, and the Sages rule it fit.
Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Shimon said one and the same thing.
Rabbi Akiva: that which we said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the ברייתא from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון share one view: an unripe אתרוג is not yet considered a fruit.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts small אתרוגים from מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows רבי שמעון's ruling: small, unripe אתרוגים are exempt from מעשרות. This means he also does not treat them as a real fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי שמעון's statement? As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון exempts אתרוגים from מעשרות while they are small.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון says this idea, and answers by quoting his ruling about מעשרות. This completes רבה's comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit needs מעשרות only once it counts as a fruit. רבי שמעון exempts small אתרוגים, so he holds they are not yet fruit. רבי עקיבא holds the same idea about the מצוה: an unripe אתרוג is not yet a 'פרי עץ הדר', so it is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A request to identify the source being referred to
Exempts. Here it means exempt from מעשרות.
While they are small and unripe

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's ruling is about מעשרות, not about the ד' מינים. רבה is pointing to the shared idea behind both rulings, not saying the two topics are the same.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה shows that רבי עקיבא (פסול for the מצוה) and רבי שמעון (exempt from מעשרות) share one idea: an unripe אתרוג is not yet a real fruit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, what is it?
As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon exempts
etrogim (from tithes) while they are small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source of רבי שמעון's view that רבה mentioned in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי שמעון matches רבי עקיבא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא where רבי שמעון exempts small אתרוגים from מעשרות, showing he does not treat them as fruit yet.

steps.title: אביי: רבי עקיבא's ruling may come only from the rule of הדר
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי עקיבא may disqualify an unripe אתרוג only because an אתרוג must be הדר (beautiful). For מעשרות, where there is no such rule, he may agree with the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Maybe that is not so. רבי עקיבא only said his ruling here, because we need the אתרוג to be הדר and this one is not. But there, regarding מעשרות, he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues against רבה's claim that רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון hold the same idea. He gives a different reason for רבי עקיבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read רבי עקיבא's ruling as saying an unripe אתרוג is not a real fruit. אביי says there is another possible reason: the מצוה needs an אתרוג that is הדר, and an unripe one is not. That reason only matters for the מצוה, so it tells us nothing about מעשרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Maybe it is not so. Used to push back against a claimed comparison or proof.
He only said it in this case. Limits a ruling to its own reason.
Beautiful. The Torah's word for the אתרוג, which requires it to look good.
Here / there. Here means the מצוה of אתרוג; there means מעשרות.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying that רבי עקיבא definitely disagrees with רבי שמעון. He only says it is possible, so רבה's link is not proven.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rabba):
Perhaps that is not so,
phrases.notes: Maybe the two תנאים do not hold the same view.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only said it here (regarding the מצוה),
because we need 'hadar' (beauty), and it is lacking,
phrases.notes: An unripe אתרוג lacks proper color and size.

phrases.english: but there (regarding tithes), he holds like the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: So an unripe אתרוג would still need מעשרות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the link that רבה made in Steps 14-15 between רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי עקיבא's ruling proves he agrees with רבי שמעון about מעשרות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא's ruling can be explained by the special requirement of הדר, which applies only to the מצוה, not by a general view that an unripe אתרוג is not a fruit.

steps.title: אביי: רבי שמעון's ruling may come only from a פסוק about מעשרות
steps.stepSummary: Another option from אביי: רבי שמעון may exempt unripe אתרוגים from מעשרות only because of a פסוק that limits מעשרות to produce that people would plant. For the מצוה of אתרוג he may agree with the רבנן that it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another option: רבי שמעון only said his ruling there, because it is written 'You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed.' This means produce that is ready the way people take it out to plant. But here, regarding the מצוה, he holds like the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second way to break רבה's link. This time he limits רבי שמעון's ruling to its own special reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about מעשרות speaks of 'the produce of your seed,' which teaches that only produce ripe enough to plant must be tithed. That is a rule just for מעשרות. So רבי שמעון could still hold, like the רבנן, that an unripe אתרוג is כשר for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively. Introduces a second possible approach.
You shall surely tithe. The פסוק about מעשרות (דברים יד:כב).
The produce of your seed. Read as produce fit for planting.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows that each תנא can be explained by a reason that only applies in his own area: הדר for the מצוה, and the פסוק of תבואת זרעך for מעשרות. So רבה's claim that רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון share one view is not proven.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. Two rulings that look alike are shown to come from different reasons, so you cannot use one תנא's view to decide another case.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon only said it there (regarding tithes),
because it is written:
'You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed,'
meaning produce ready the way people take it out for sowing.
phrases.notes: Unripe fruit is not fit to plant, so it is exempt.

phrases.english: But here (regarding the מצוה), he holds like the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: So an unripe אתרוג would be כשר for the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate way for אביי to reject רבה's link, this time by limiting רבי שמעון's ruling instead of רבי עקיבא's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רבי שמעון's מעשרות ruling proves he agrees with רבי עקיבא about the מצוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון's exemption comes from a פסוק that applies only to מעשרות, not from a general view that an unripe אתרוג is not a fruit.
